_doc: Layer registry: the top level of the data taxonomy. Layer -> Group -> Metric. Adding a data domain means adding a layer here; the app builds its navigation from the manifest and needs no code change.

_kinds.metric: Choropleth data. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE -- exactly one metric colors the map at a time, because a polygon has one fill. Selecting a new metric replaces the current one.
_kinds.overlay: Drawn on top of the choropleth. ADDITIVE -- any number can be visible at once (neighborhood outlines + transit lines + parks). Overlays carry no index/baseline; they are geometry plus labels, not measurements.

layers.label: Census & Demographics
layers.description: American Community Survey 5-year estimates. Annual, small-area, survey-based -- every value carries a margin of error.

provider.name: US Census Bureau
provider.attribution: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates

layers.label: Politics & Elections
layers.description: Certified presidential general election returns by county, 2000-2024. Election geography is precincts, which nest inside nothing this project draws -- not tracts, not townships, not places. The COUNTY is the canvassing unit everywhere, so it is the finest geography where returns and census polygons describe the same ground without interpolation.

provider.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab
provider.attribution: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, County Presidential Election Returns 2000-2024

layers._license_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-02 from the Dataverse dataset metadata: CC0 1.0, not CC-BY as this entry previously claimed. MEDSL still asks to be cited, which is what provider.attribution is for.
layers._geography_note: 'precinct' is deliberately NOT listed. Precinct returns exist (VEST, doi:10.7910/DVN/K7760H) but would need geometry per election cycle, carry no stable ids across years, and join to no other metric in this project -- the scatter and the baseline picker would both go dark there. Sub-county politics wants the block-disaggregation route instead; see docs/data-sources.md.

layers.label: Climate & Weather
layers.description: NOAA historical summaries. Station POINTS, not polygons -- values must be interpolated onto areas before they can be a choropleth, and that interpolation is an estimate that has to be disclosed.

provider.name: NOAA NCEI
provider.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

layers.label: Columbus Neighborhoods
layers.description: The city's own 41 community areas -- Clintonville, German Village, Franklinton, the University District. Display only: they follow streets and rivers, not tract lines, so no statistic is recomputed onto them. Covers the city of Columbus only; suburbs are named by the City / Suburb geography instead.
layers._license_note: VERIFIED 2026-08-31 from the portal item metadata: license CC0-1.0 / licenseInfo CC0. Previously recorded as unknown-check-before-publishing.
layers._source_note: Layer 25, 'Columbus Communities'. Deliberately NOT layer 12, 'Area Commissions': that one covers only part of the city (21 polygons vs 41) and its attribute table carries volunteer names, personal emails and phone numbers, none of which belongs in a public static bundle.

layers.label: Places & Infrastructure
layers.description: Parks, transit, schools from OpenStreetMap via Overpass. Extracted at build time only -- Overpass is heavily rate-limited and must never be called from the browser.
